54269-a-letter-to-the-rev-william-maskel.title: Rev. William Maskell, A.M.
54269-a-letter-to-the-rev-william-maskel.creator: Unknown
54269-a-letter-to-the-rev-william-maskel.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Let me, however, here say in the very outset, I am not by any means about to attempt an answer to your letter; a task for which I am, in the first place, not qualified, and in the second place, not disposed. I feel the difficulties you bring forward too much myself to be prepared to ignore them, though I will not say I go with you in the whole of the positions you are concerned to establish.

arabian-nights-burton-1885-vol-09.title: The Book of the Thousand Nights and a Night, Vol. 9
arabian-nights-burton-1885-vol-09.creator: Richard F. Burton (trans.)
arabian-nights-burton-1885-vol-09.description: Vol. 9 of Sir Richard Burton's unexpurgated 1885 literal translation of the Alf Layla wa Layla — the most famous and most cited English rendering of the Arabian Nights, with Burton's terminal essay and notes. Public domain. Sourced from Project Gutenberg ebook #55587 (https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/55587).

arxiv-1701-06238.title: Synthetic geometry of differential equations: I. Jets and comonad structure.
arxiv-1701-06238.creator: Igor Khavkine and Urs Schreiber
arxiv-1701-06238.description: Abstract We give an abstract formulation of the formal theory partial differential equations (PDEs) in synthetic differential geometry, one that would seamlessly generalize the traditional theory to a range of enhanced contexts, such as super-geometry, higher (stacky) differential geometry, or even a combination of both.

arxiv-1805-11185.title: K2 Ultracool Dwarfs Survey. IV. Monster flares observed on the young brown dwarf CFHT-BD-Tau 4. :
arxiv-1805-11185.creator: Rishi R. Paudel, John E. Gizis, D. J. Mullan, Sarah J. Schmidt, Adam J. Burgasser, Peter K. G. Williams, Edo Berger
arxiv-1805-11185.description: Abstract We present photometric measurements of two superflares observed on a very young brown dwarf CFHT-BD-Tau 4, observed during Campaign 13 of the Kepler K2 mission. The stronger of the two superflares brightened by a factor of ∼ \sim 48 relative to the quiescent photospheric level, with an increase in Kepler magnitude Δ ​ K p ~ \Delta\tilde{K_{p}} = -4.20.

arxiv-2104-11144.title: Folded and contracted solutions of coupled classical dynamical Yang-Baxter and reflection equations
arxiv-2104-11144.creator: Jasper V. Stokman
arxiv-2104-11144.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jasper V. Stokman. In this paper we give a concrete recipe how to construct triples of algebra-valued meromorphic functions on a complex vector space 𝔞 \mathfrak{a} satisfying three coupled classical dynamical Yang-Baxter equations and an associated classical dynamical reflection equation. Such triples provide the local factors of a consistent system of first order differential operators on 𝔞 \mathfrak{a} , generalising asymptotic boundary Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov-Bernard (KZB) equations.

arxiv-2105-13536.title: ECG HEART-BEAT CLASSIFICATION USING MULTIMODAL IMAGE FUSION
arxiv-2105-13536.creator: Zeeshan Ahmad, Anika Tabassum, Ling Guan, Naimul Khan
arxiv-2105-13536.description: Abstract In this paper, we present a novel Image Fusion Model (IFM) for ECG heart-beat classification to overcome the weaknesses of existing machine learning techniques that rely either on manual feature extraction or direct utilization of 1D raw ECG signal.

arxiv-2202-12614.title: Dynamic Traffic Allocation in IEEE 802.11be Multi-link WLANs
arxiv-2202-12614.creator: Álvaro López-Raventós, Boris Bellalta
arxiv-2202-12614.description: Abstract The multi-link operation (MLO) is a key feature of the next IEEE 802.11be Extremely High Throughput amendment. Through its adoption, it is expected to enhance users’ experience by improving throughput rates and latency. However, potential MLO gains are tied to how traffic is distributed across the multiple radio interfaces.

arxiv-2206-07137.title: Prioritized Training on Points that are Learnable, Worth Learning, and Not Yet Learnt
arxiv-2206-07137.creator: Sören Mindermann, Jan Brauner, Muhammed Razzak, Mrinank Sharma, Andreas Kirsch, Winnie Xu, Benedikt Höltgen, Aidan N. Gomez, Adrien Morisot, Sebastian Farquhar, Yarin Gal
arxiv-2206-07137.description: Abstract Training on web-scale data can take months. But most computation and time is wasted on redundant and noisy points that are already learnt or not learnable. To accelerate training, we introduce Reducible Holdout Loss Selection (RHO-LOSS), a simple but principled technique which selects approximately those points for training that most reduce the model’s generalization loss.

arxiv-2207-01048.title: A Formal Framework for Distributed Cyber-Physical Systems
arxiv-2207-01048.creator: Benjamin Lion, Farhad Arbab, Carolyn Talcott
arxiv-2207-01048.description: Abstract Composition is an important feature of a specification language, as it enables the design of a complex system in terms of a product of its parts. Decomposition is equally important in order to reason about structural properties of a system.

arxiv-2403-16811.title: Cross section measurement of e + ​ e − → η ​ ψ ​ ( 𝟐 ​ S ) e^{+}e^{-}\to\eta\psi(2S) and search for e + ​ e − → η ​ X ~ ​ ( 𝟑𝟖𝟕𝟐 ) e^{+}e^{-}\to\eta\tilde{X}(3872)
arxiv-2403-16811.creator: M. Ablikim 1 , M. N. Achasov 4,c , P. Adlarson 75 , O. Afedulidis 3 , X. C. Ai 80 , R. Aliberti 35 , A. Amoroso 74A,74C , Q. An 71,58,a , Y. Bai 57 , O. Bakina 36 , I. Balossino 29A , Y. Ban 46,h , H.-R. Bao 63 , V. Batozskaya 1,44 , K. Begzsuren 32 , N. Berger 35 , M. Berlowski 44 , M. Bertani 28A
arxiv-2403-16811.description: Abstract The energy-dependent cross section for e + ​ e − → η ​ ψ ​ ( 2 ​ S ) e^{+}e^{-}\to\eta\psi(2S) is measured at eighteen center of mass energies from 4.288 GeV to 4.951 GeV using the BESIII detector.

arxiv-2407-13405.title: Unveiling the nonlinear dynamics of a rolling axion during inflation
arxiv-2407-13405.creator: Angelo Caravano, Marco Peloso
arxiv-2407-13405.description: Abstract A spectator axion-gauge sector, minimally coupled to the inflaton, with the axion experiencing a momentary stage of fast roll during cosmological inflation, can generate unique signatures in primordial density fluctuations and the gravitational wave background. We present the first lattice simulation of this system using a novel hybrid numerical scheme.

arxiv-2408-05852.title: Characterisation of the stellar wind in Cyg X-1 via modelling of colour-colour diagrams
arxiv-2408-05852.creator: E. V. Lai, B. De Marco, Y. Cavecchi, I. El Mellah, M. Cinus, C. M. Diez, V. Grinberg, A. A. Zdziarski, P. Uttley, M. Bachetti, J. José, G. Sala, A. Różańska, J. Wilms
arxiv-2408-05852.description: Abstract Context. Cygnus X-1 is a high mass X-ray binary where accretion onto the black hole is mediated by the stellar wind from the blue supergiant companion star HDE 226868. Due to its inclination, the system is a perfect laboratory to study the not yet well-understood stellar wind structure.

arxiv-2409-18121.title: Robot See Robot Do: Imitating Articulated Object Manipulation with Monocular 4D Reconstruction
arxiv-2409-18121.creator: Justin Kerr Chung Min Kim Mingxuan Wu Brent Yi
arxiv-2409-18121.description: Abstract Humans can learn to manipulate new objects by simply watching others; providing robots with the ability to learn from such demonstrations would enable a natural interface specifying new behaviors. This work develops Robot See Robot Do (RSRD), a method for imitating articulated object manipulation from a single monocular RGB human demonstration given a single static multi-view object scan.

arxiv-2409-19629.title: A Survey on Graph Neural Networks for Remaining Useful Life Prediction: Methodologies, Evaluation and Future Trends
arxiv-2409-19629.creator: Yucheng Wang, Min Wu, Xiaoli Li, Lihua Xie, Zhenghua Chen
arxiv-2409-19629.description: Abstract Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction is a critical aspect of Prognostics and Health Management (PHM), aimed at predicting the future state of a system to enable timely maintenance and prevent unexpected failures. While existing deep learning methods have shown promise, they often struggle to fully leverage the spatial information inherent in complex systems, limiting their effectiveness in RUL prediction.

arxiv-2412-20203.title: No-Regret Learning in Harmonic Games: Extrapolation in the Face of Conflicting Interests Thanks: The authors are grateful to Victor Boone and Marco Scarsini for fruitful discussions.
arxiv-2412-20203.creator: Davide Legacci c,∗, Panayotis Mertikopoulos ∗, Christos H. Papadimitriou ⋄,♯, Georgios Piliouras ¶, Bary S. R. Pradelski §
arxiv-2412-20203.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Davide Legacci c,∗, Panayotis Mertikopoulos ∗, Christos H. Papadimitriou ⋄,♯, Georgios Piliouras ¶, Bary S. R. Pradelski §. The long-run behavior of multi-agent learning – and, in particular, no-regret learning – is relatively well-understood in potential games, where players have aligned interests. By contrast, in harmonic games – the strategic counterpart of potential games, where players have conflicting interests – very little is known outside the narrow subclass of 2 2 -player zero-sum games with a fully-mixed equilibrium.

arxiv-2505-03029.title: An Exact Turbulence Law For the Fluid Description of Fusion Edge Plasmas
arxiv-2505-03029.creator: L. Scarivaglione, S. Servidio
arxiv-2505-03029.description: Abstract Understanding turbulence via simplified fluid models is crucial for optimizing magnetic confinement in tokamak devices. In this work, we propose a novel high-order turbulence law that describes the turbulent cascade at the edges of fusion plasmas, namely valid within the Scrape-off Layer (SOL), in the framework of the Braginskii fluid model.

arxiv-2604-13817.creator: Tao Wang, Jingyao Lu, Xibo Wang, Haonan Huang, Su Yao, Zhiqiang Hu, Xingyan Chen, Enmao Diao

arxiv-2606-19938.creator: Yi Xiao, Carlos Rodriguez Coronel, Jing Zhan, Haniyeh Ehsani Oskouie, Alex Wong, Dong Lao, Correspondence to

pmc-11328431.title: Translation and psychometric validation of the Patient Participation Culture Tool for healthcare workers in Chinese nursing context
pmc-11328431.creator: Wenna Wang, Shanshan Wang, Qianqian Sun, Zhenxiang Zhang, Chenxi Zhou, Qiushi Zhang, Yongxia Mei
pmc-11328431.description: BackgroundPromoting patient participation stands as a global priority in nursing care. Currently, there is a lack of a standardized tool to assess the culture of patient participation from the perspective of nurses in China.AimsTo translate and examine the validity and reliability of the Patient Participation Culture Tool for healthcare workers (PaCT-HCW) on general hospital wards in Chinese nursing context.

pmc-11469415.title: Construction of a prediction model for hepatic encephalopathy in acute-on-chronic liver failure patients
pmc-11469415.creator: Shenglong Lin, Xiangmei Wang, Zixin Xu, Lu Li, Rui Kang, Songtao Li, Xiaoyong Wu, Yueyong Zhu, Haibing Gao
pmc-11469415.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectiveHepatic encephalopathy (HE) is a serious complication of acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) that requires early detection and intervention to positively impact patient prognosis. This study aimed to develop a reliable model to predict HE in ACLF patients during hospitalization.MethodsRetrospectively recruiting 255 hepatitis B-related ACLF patients, including 67 who developed HE during hospitalization, the study analysed clinical data and biochemical indices collected during the first week of admission.

pmc-11508853.title: Clinical Significance of Perinephric Fluid Collection in Patients with Renal Colic and Urolithiasis: A Retrospective Analysis
pmc-11508853.creator: Stefano Moretto, Ugo Gradilone, Giovanni Costanzi Porrini, Marco Montesi, Antonio Cretì, Pierluigi Russo, Filippo Marino, Nazario Foschi, Marcello Covino, Francesco Pinto, Mauro Ragonese, Jean De la Rosette
pmc-11508853.description: Background: Perinephric fluid is commonly identified in patients with renal colic and urolithiasis, especially in cases associated with hydronephrosis. However, its clinical relevance, particularly its impact on treatment decisions and prognosis, is not well established. Methods: This retrospective, single-center study included adult patients who presented to the emergency department (ED) with suspected renal colic between January 2021 and October 2023.

pmc-11665611.title: A wideband CPW slot antenna by using conductor-backed coplanar feeding
pmc-11665611.creator: Yulei Xue, Ruiqiang Yan, Weiping Huang, Yanchen Dong
pmc-11665611.description: In this paper, a new wideband coplanar waveguide (CPW) rhomboid slot antenna by using conductor-backed coplanar waveguide (CBCPW) feeding, which works at 4.6 GHz with a relative impedance bandwidth of about 55.6 %, and a gain of more than 5.

pmc-11675751.title: Evaluating the Role of CBC-Derived Indices in Children with Hashimoto’s Thyroiditis
pmc-11675751.creator: Andrei-Ioan Munteanu, Iulius Jugănaru, Delia-Maria Nicoară, Niculina Mang, Raluca Vasilescu, Giorgiana-Flavia Brad, Alexandra-Cristina Scutca, Raluca Asproniu, Lucian-Ioan Cristun, Otilia Mărginean
pmc-11675751.description: Background/Objectives: Hashimoto’s thyroiditis (HT) is an autoimmune disorder characterized by chronic inflammation of the thyroid gland. Recent evidence indicates that the inflammation may extend beyond the thyroid. The study aims to explore the potential of complete blood count (CBC)-derived indices as markers of systemic inflammation in HT.

pmc-11715729.title: Chronic Medical Conditions and Dementia Risk: Brain Age Models for Quantifying Impact and Understanding Mechanisms
pmc-11715729.creator: Xi Yu, Scott A. Przybelski, Robert I. Reid, Robel K Gebre, Timothy G. Lesnick, Maria Vassilaki, Jonathan Graff‐Radford, David S. Knopman, Ronald C. Petersen, Clifford R. Jack, Prashanthi Vemuri
pmc-11715729.description: BackgroundChronic medical conditions increase dementia risk, and the mechanism may be captured computationally by measures of accelerated brain aging. We hypothesized that quantifying the impact of chronic conditions on GM and WM aging will aid in measuring the differential impact of each condition on brain aging and shed light on the mechanisms through which they increase dementia risk.

pmc-11716221.title: Associations of plasma phospho‐Tau217 with amyloid‐PET and cognitive status in adults with Down syndrome
pmc-11716221.creator: Brecca Bettcher, Shorena Janelidze, Max McLachlan, Matthew D Zammit, Andrew K McVea, Alexandra H DiFilippo, Tobey J. Betthauser, Charles M Laymon, Dana Tudorascu, Annie Cohen, Arun Garimella, Julie C Price, David B. Keator, Adam M. Brickman, Patrick J. Lao, William E Klunk, H. Diana Rosas, Shahid Za
pmc-11716221.description: BackgroundBlood‐based biomarkers able to detect atypical neuropathology could serve as a cost‐effective and noninvasive screening to include participants with Down syndrome (DS) in anti‐amyloid clinical trials. Accurately placing these novel biomarkers on the AD pathological cascade as proposed by the AT(N) framework informs relative disease progression of individuals.

pmc-12502900.title: Exploring the Impact of the 2020 COVID‐19 Adjusted Lockdown on Social Workers at a Gender‐Based Violence Command Centre in Pretoria, Gauteng
pmc-12502900.creator: Qebo Ignatia Nkosi, Leane Ramsoomar
pmc-12502900.description: IntroductionIn South Africa and across many regions globally, adjusted lockdowns were implemented as a measure to curb the spread of COVID‐19. These lockdowns had a significant effect on gender‐based violence (GBV). Victims, often confined with their abusers, faced limited access to support services.

pmc-12512299.title: Smoking and the risk of prostate cancer: a review of risk and disease progression
pmc-12512299.creator: Ishvaria Sundaresan, Nallasivam Palanisamy, Radha Saraswathy
pmc-12512299.description: BackgroundProstate cancer is still the most common malignancy affecting men worldwide, with causes ranging from genetics to environmental and lifestyle factors. This review narrows its attention to investigate smoking as a risk factor for the start and progression of prostate cancer.

pmc-12948670.title: Disordered eating, oral health and sports
pmc-12948670.creator: Rebecca Moazzez, Deborah Bomfim, Renee McGregor, Rupert Austin
pmc-12948670.description: Multiple studies have identified that eating disorders are more common in elite athletes than in non-athlete populations. There are a wide range of types of eating disorders that can impact the oral and general health of athletes, including anorexia, bulimia, binge eating disorder, avoidant restrictive food intake disorder and other specified feeding and eating disorder.

pmc-12976279.title: Prevalence and Causes of Acute Kidney Injury and Chronic Kidney Disease in Ghana: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-12976279.creator: Justice Afrifa, Kennedy Asum, Samuel Aidoo Bervell Fosu, Blessing Owusu Gyamfi, Nathaniel Laryea Ayerkain, Michael Gyamfi Oti, Stephanie Taylor, Perditer Okyere, Ibrahim Anyass Goumboundi, Richard K. D. Ephraim
pmc-12976279.description: BackgroundAcute kidney injury (AKI) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) are major contributors to morbidity and mortality globally, with a growing burden in sub-Saharan Africa. In Ghana, kidney disease is increasingly recognized as a public health concern; however, pooled data on its prevalence and etiology is absent.

pmc-13138324.title: Linking miRNAs to decay
pmc-13138324.creator: Amy E. Pasquinelli
pmc-13138324.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In this Outlook, Pasquinelli discusses a study in this issue of Genes & Development by Grimme et al. that identifies lncRNA tts-2 as a potent trigger RNA for target-directed miRNA degradation of the miR-35-42 family. Pasquinelli highlights how this study expands on our understanding of the base-pairing requirements between trigger RNAs and their target miRNAs for the effective regulation of miRNA abundance.

pmc-13330771.title: Comprehensive characterization and recovery of nickel, cobalt, cerium, and lanthanum from nickel–metal hydride batteries through bioleaching of spent medium by Acidithiobacillus thiooxidans
pmc-13330771.creator: Zoha Heidarinejad, Mahdi Farzadkia, Seyyed Mohammad Mousavi, Mitra Gholami, Roshanak Rezaei Kalantary
pmc-13330771.description: Although lithium-ion batteries receive widespread focus, managing and reducing the environmental risks posed by spent nickel–metal hydride (Ni–MH) batteries is still a significant global issue. Choosing a sustainable and eco-friendly method for these batteries is challenging due to their complexity.

pmc-13490589.title: Artificial intelligence enabled performance evaluation of an enhanced SPR biosensor for malaria diagnosis
pmc-13490589.creator: Md. Al Amin Islam Utshob, Maymona Binte Juwel, Khandakar Mohammad Ishtiak, Aminur Rahman, M. M. Atiqur Rahman, Safayat-Al Imam, S. M. Ishraqul Huq, Quazi D. M. Khosru
pmc-13490589.description: Malaria remains a serious global health problem, particularly in areas where drug-resistant Plasmodium species and the expanded geographical distribution of malaria caused by climate change are of concern. In response to the pressing need for a rapid and highly sensitive malaria diagnostic method, this paper proposes a novel surface plasmon resonance (SPR) biosensor design with a multilayer N-FK51a+SiO2+Cu+HfO2+BP structure.

uslaw-usc-t36-s152305.description: United States Code, Title 36 (Patriotic And National Observances, Ceremonies, And Organizations); Part B (Organizations); Chapter 1523 (National Music Council). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel.
